beats.narration: Begin by framing Search Engine Architecture Overview as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. An introduction to the theories and techniques used to construct search engines. Consider this worked case: A web crawler indexes HTML pages by extracting text, building an inverted index, and storing term frequencies. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Search Engine Architecture Overview
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a flowchart showing query input, index lookup, and result output with labeled components.

beats.narration: Now define Query Processing and Parsing precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Queries select, join, aggregate, order, and transform data. Consider this worked case: A natural language query like 'climate change effects' is tokenized and normalized to match indexed terms. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Query Processing and Parsing
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a side-by-side comparison of raw query text versus parsed query components with highlighted tokens.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Inverted Index Construction operates in a concrete sequence. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected workloads. Consider this worked case: The term 'machine' points to document IDs [101, 105, 112], allowing direct access to containing pages. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Inverted Index Construction
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a simplified inverted index table with term columns and document ID lists.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in TF-IDF Relevance Scoring and make the decision criteria explicit. Topics include search interfaces, traditional retrieval models (for example, TF-IDF, BM25), modern retrieval techniques (for example, neural reranking and retrieval), search engine evaluation, and search applications (for example, conversational IR, enterprise search). Consider this worked case: A term appearing in many documents receives a lower IDF weight, reducing its relevance score. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: TF-IDF Relevance Scoring
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate TF-IDF calculation with a small document corpus showing term frequencies and IDF values.

beats.narration: Apply BM25 Ranking Algorithm to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Students may not take and receive credit for CSCI-536 and CSCI-636. Consider this worked case: Short documents receive higher scores for rare terms, while BM25 adjusts scores based on term position in text. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: BM25 Ranking Algorithm
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a comparison table of TF-IDF versus BM25 scores for the same query across different documents.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Neural Reranking Techniques, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Data-analysis workflows separate data preparation, exploratory analysis, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Consider this worked case: A transformer-based model scores query-document pairs by analyzing semantic similarity in high-dimensional space. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Neural Reranking Techniques
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a neural network diagram with query and document embeddings merging into a relevance score output.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Search Evaluation Metrics with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Query planning and physical storage affect performance without changing logical query meaning. Consider this worked case: Precision measures the fraction of retrieved documents that are relevant, while NDCG accounts for ranking order. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Search Evaluation Metrics
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a precision-recall curve and NDCG graph with labeled axes and example points.

beats.narration: Use Conversational and Enterprise Search to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Students will also review current IR research topics, and complete a group project in which they will design and execute experiments for search engine components. Consider this worked case: Enterprise search indexes internal documents with role-based access and contextual filters for business users. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Conversational and Enterprise Search
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a dialogue flow for conversational search and a dashboard for enterprise search filters.

beats.narration: Connect Experimental Design in IR to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Supervised methods learn mappings from examples paired with target labels, while unsupervised methods identify structure without targets. Consider this worked case: A group project tests BM25 versus neural reranking on a benchmark corpus to measure score improvements. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Experimental Design in IR
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display an experimental setup diagram with baseline, variant, and evaluation metrics.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Evaluation must match the task and the cost of errors, while distribution shift, missing data, overfitting, and unexamined sampling choices can invalidate conclusions. Consider this worked case: The checklist verifies index coverage, ranking consistency, metric alignment, and error cost assessment. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a printable checklist template with checkboxes for each evaluation criterion.

sources.excerpt: Data systems organize records with declared types, tables, rows, columns, keys, and constraints. Queries select, join, aggregate, order, and transform data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected workloads. Transactions group operations and isolation controls how concurrent operations observe one another. Query planning and physical storage affect performance without changing logical query meaning. Analytical work should preserve provenance from captured data through cleaning, transformation, grouping, modeling, visualization, and reporting. Data quality analysis makes missingness, duplicates, inconsistent representation, integrity constraints, sampling, and update behavior explicit.
